HEEWON WEBTOON — a KOREAN WEBTOON character-introduction splash used as a movie still, bold manhwa cover finish (Solo Leveling, Omniscient Reader). A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (medium close, two-shot, three-shot, split) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, dutch), never a flat catalogue pose, never a photoreal landscape with tiny people. LINE: THICK, confident black ink contours with real line weight — a heavy tapered outline around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands; solid black spot-blacks fill the deepest shadows, the hair masses and the insides of sleeves. SHADING: cel-shaded in hard-edged shapes — a base tone, ONE crisp shadow shape and one small sharp highlight per surface, at most one soft gradient for form; glossy graphic highlights on hair, eyes, lacquer and steel. Clean saturated colour. NOT painterly brushwork, NOT watercolor, NOT soft sketchy lines, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. CHARACTER DESIGN: a DESIGNED character, never a generic handsome manhwa face — the face shape, eye shape, brows, nose, mouth, build and posture below belong to this person and no one else, pushed far enough that they read at thumbnail size and in silhouette alone. KOREAN FACES: these are 7th-century Koreans, drawn the way the best Korean webtoons draw Koreans — living eyes with WHITE sclera, a catchlight, and BLACK ink-black iris and pupil (never brown, hazel, amber, blue, grey or green, never the whole eyeball painted solid black), East Asian bone structure, single-lidded or low-creased eyes, straight or softly arched brows, a low soft Korean nasal bridge (never a high European nose), broad cheekbones, flatter facial planes, warm ivory to sun-browned skin, straight coarse black hair; varied from person to person (moon faces, long faces, square jaws), never Western, Latin or mixed-race features, never deep-set double-lidded western eyes, never the interchangeable pretty anime face. Keep identity from the attached sheet (hair, dress, colours, ornaments) but REDRAW the person in this bolder style; the sheet's soft sketchy rendering is not the style. OVERRIDE: if a note says photoreal-numinous, IGNORE it — REDRAW every face as webtoon ink. The attached portraits of Big Star and Little Star are photographs of actors: copy hair colour, clothes colours and bone structure ONLY. NEVER photographic skin, pores, live-action lighting, or camera grain. Faces LARGE in the central band. INTRO-CARD WEBTOON two-shot, faces LARGE. PRIMORDIAL ink-brush aura. NIGHT, Land of the Dead as graphic black, not a photographed valley. Worm’s-eye. ONE DEVICE: an empty timber bench with an ice-blue seam. LEFT = Big Star sitting on the bench, testing it, black po, ice-blue collar — photograph: REDRAW as webtoon. SECOND = Haewonmek mid-stride at the right third, gat brim, black robe, blue sash, walking away down the hall, mouth only. One of each, never clone. #3B6FBF on the bench; #6b5b6e on the robe. Thick ink, cel shadow. Not photoreal. REFERENCE SHEET. TOP ROW, left to right: LEFT face = daebyeol, SECOND face = haewonmek. Identity only (hair, clothes, bones); REDRAW as webtoon, never photographic skin. BACKGROUND: big graphic shapes and ink-wash, not a photographed place — two or three flat value planes, splashed sumi ink (pomuk) and dry-brush flying-white at the frame edges, paper grain, the world dissolving into Joseon ink at the margins. LIGHT: ONE hard key; each character's hex lives in that light, never a glow aura. ACTING: big readable manhwa faces. New poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. NOT photoreal, NOT oil-portrait, NOT live-action. NIGHT GROUND: the frame is built on BLACK — crushed ink-black night masses around the subject, the place pulled out of the dark only where the one key light (fire, lamp, torch, moon) falls, small warm bokeh in the black; the figure is the bright thing in a dark frame.
